rationale: Scores and ranks every application against the vacancy; recruiters see the ranked list first. Filtering applications is named in Annex III 4(a), and ranking people on their profile is profiling, so the Article 6(3) derogation cannot apply.

The job board decides who sees each advert from users' profiles, with no one reviewing who is shown it. Placing targeted job advertisements is named in Annex III 4(a); the employer chooses the audience settings, so it controls part of the input.

A pilot in Barcelona scores recorded interviews on tone of voice and facial expressions. Inferring emotions in the workplace is prohibited unless for medical or safety reasons, and candidates in a selection process fall within it: the use has to stop.

Proposes interview slots from calendars once a recruiter has shortlisted a candidate. Part of a recruitment process, but a narrow procedural task that profiles no one: Article 6(3)(a). It talks to candidates by email, so Article 50(1) applies to its provider.

Scores each agent weekly on handling time, resolution and sentiment of the customer's words, and flags low performers to team leads. Monitoring and evaluating performance is named in Annex III 4(b); scoring individuals is profiling.

Allocates shifts in the warehouses from each worker's certified skills, availability and past attendance, and publishes the rota unless a supervisor steps in. Allocating tasks on individual behaviour or characteristics is named in Annex III 4(b), and past attendance makes it profiling. A boundary case: on availability alone it might not be.

Built by HR analytics on the people data (see hr-people-analytics): a risk score per employee that managers use to plan retention conversations and counter-offers. It evaluates individuals and shapes decisions on terms of work, so it is high-risk, and because the employer put it into service for its own use, the employer is its provider (Art. 3(3) and (11)).

The compensation module proposes each employee's merit increase from rating, compa-ratio and market data; managers accept or edit. Decisions affecting terms of work-related relationships are named in Annex III 4(b). Its pay-setting criteria must also be objective and gender-neutral under the Pay Transparency Directive (Articles 4(4) and 6(1)).

Answers employees' questions on leave, payroll and policies from the knowledge base, and hands over to an HR advisor. It decides nothing about anyone, so it is not in Annex III; people must know they are talking to an AI (Article 50(1)).

Suggests courses from role and past courses. Annex III point 3 covers education and vocational training institutions, not an employer's course suggestions; completion has no bearing on promotion or pay in this organisation. If it did, the system would move into Annex III 4(b).
A general-purpose assistant HR staff use to draft and translate letters and policies, reviewed before sending. Minimal risk; the staff who use it are within the AI literacy duty.
Matches employees to internal vacancies and ranks internal candidates for the hiring manager. Selection is named in Annex III 4(a), and ranking people on their profile is profiling.
